description: Audit given PHP file(s)/scope for complete, well-formed PHPDoc — class/interface/trait/enum docblocks, public and protected methods and properties, constants, generics and array shapes (`@template`, `@extends`/`@implements`, `list<T>`, `array<K, V>`, `array{...}`, `class-string<T>`, `non-empty-string`), and `@throws` — generate any missing or incomplete docblocks grounded in the actual code and current changes, without duplicating what native type declarations already say, then verify the result with the project's own tooling: PHPStan (which rejects invalid PHPDoc types and docblocks that contradict native types; Psalm when that's the project's analyser), the WordPress-Docs/Squiz commenting sniffs of PHP_CodeSniffer when configured, the project's Pint/PHP-CS-Fixer `phpdoc_*` rules, and phpDocumentor when the project has it (`phpdoc.dist.xml`/`phpdoc.xml` or `vendor/bin/phpdoc`). Flavor-aware: Laravel and plain libraries follow the PHPStan-typed "don't repeat native types" convention; WordPress plugins/themes follow the WordPress PHP inline documentation standards (file headers, `@since`, full `@param`/`@return` tags, hook docblocks with one `@param` per argument before every `do_action()`/`apply_filters()`); PrestaShop modules follow PrestaShop's conventions (docblocks on classes, properties, and methods regardless of visibility — the license header block itself is `iru-check-license`'s job, not this skill's). Invoke as `/iru-php-phpdoc <path-or-glob>` (comma-separated paths/globs accepted), or `/iru-php-phpdoc` with no argument to scope to PHP files touched by uncommitted changes plus commits on the current branch not yet on the base branch. Use whenever the user wants PHPDoc completeness checked and filled in for specific files, instead of relying on a full static-analysis or docs build to surface gaps.
